key_insight: Machine learning acceptance in life sciences is shaped not just by usefulness and ease of use, but also by perceived hype and journal impact factor as credibility signals.
clinical_relevance: For biomedical teams considering ML tools, perceived scientific legitimacy and organizational trust may matter as much as technical performance when driving adoption.
method: Cross-sectional quantitative survey of 213 biomedical and life science professionals
Regions covered: EMEA, LATAM, and North America
Extended TAM tested with PLS-SEM and external variables
evidence_signal: The study used survey data and PLS-SEM to test an extended technology acceptance model in a life sciences workforce sample.
watch_item: Because the design is cross-sectional and perception-based, the findings can show association but not prove that hype or journal impact factor causes adoption.
paper_title: Technology acceptance of machine learning in life sciences: the role of hype perception and journal impact factor.
